- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >80), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and prices are falling, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon; apply a 2–4% downward correction for days 1–7.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from positive to negative), model often lags; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift, especially in days 8–14.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day window; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
